subject: RE: ACME POC - Integration plan, success criteria, and next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Johnson <alice.johnson@acme.com>, Tom Wu <tom.wu@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: ACME POC - Integration plan, success criteria, and next steps

Thanks again for the call this morning — great conversation. Per our discussion, here’s a concise recap and proposed plan so we can get the POC started quickly. Please confirm or update the success criteria and the timelines below.

1) Success criteria (what Acme will use to evaluate the POC)
- End-to-end throughput: support 50 concurrent user sessions with median response latency < 800ms (95th < 1.5s) for 2k token requests.
- Quality: > 90% correctness on the provided evaluation set (see link to test prompts).
- Feature coverage: streaming responses for long-form assistant, function/tool calling for internal product APIs, and embedding generation for search re-ranking.
- Operational: metrics and logs visible in Redwood Console; token-level cost estimate within agreed budget.

2) Evaluation plan and timeline
- 2026-10-20: Kickoff + environment handoff (test API key, sample dataset).
- 2026-10-21 to 2026-10-26: Integration period (SDK + API routes, streaming enabled, function calling wiring).
- 2026-10-27 to 2026-10-30: Internal testing and evaluation run by Acme; Redwood to monitor and troubleshoot.
- 2026-11-02: Goal: decision on expansion / next steps.

3) Ownership (proposed)
- Redwood: Marissa (program lead), Dylan (engineering lead for integration), Lauren (QA & rollout support).
- Acme: Alice (ML lead), Tom (platform lead).

4) Integration checklist (items we agreed on)
- Provide a test account + sample dataset from Acme.
- SDK install and initial generate/stream examples (Python + Node).
- API routes: /v1/generate (sync), /v1/streams (SSE), support for function calling JSON schema.
- Auth: API keys for the POC (support for mTLS if needed for Private deployment later).
- Telemetry: grant Redwood read access to a minimal set of logs/metrics for troubleshooting.

Attachments: acme_poc_integration_diagram.png (image/png), redwood_sdk_sample_code.patch (text/x-patch)
Links: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/poc-acme-integration-plan, HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.com/deal/ACME-2026-POC-43

Ask from Acme: please confirm the success criteria above and whether 10/20 works for kickoff. Also confirm whether you can provide the test dataset and a test account with the expected traffic shape.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0186
From: Alice Johnson <alice.johnson@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Tom Wu <tom.wu@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Oct 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ACME POC - Integration plan, success criteria, and next steps

Thanks Marissa — that looks good and aligns with what we discussed. A few quick additions from our side:
- Confirmed: success criteria look right. We may tighten the correctness metric based on a small pilot, but the 90% baseline is fine.
- Security: we’ll need a short security questionnaire (SOC2 evidence) and an IP allowlist for the test endpoints.
- Data: we can provide a sanitized dataset (10k prompts) and a test account by EOD 2026-10-19.
- Technical asks: can you share function calling examples (JSON schema + sample payload) and streaming sample (SSE or websocket)? Also include the SDK snippets for Python and Node.

2026-10-20 kickoff at 10:00 PT works from my side. Please loop in your engineering lead so we can discuss the API routes and any rate-limiting considerations.

Appreciate it,
Alice Johnson
Senior ML Engineer | Acme Corp
alice.johnson@acme.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alice Johnson <alice.johnson@acme.com>, Tom Wu <tom.wu@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Oct 2026 13:15:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: ACME POC - Integration plan, success criteria, and next steps

Forwarding Alice’s confirmation and the POC checklist. Dylan / Lauren — can you propose a short implementation plan and ETA on the engineering tasks below? Ideally we respond to Acme today with the requested examples and a brief timeline so they can start prepping the dataset.

Key items to include in your plan:
- SDK examples: Python and Node minimal install + generate + stream + function-calling example.
- API endpoints for POC: /v1/generate (sync), /v1/streams (SSE streaming), /v1/embeddings, function-calling contract endpoint.
- Auth & security: API key for POC; note on mTLS/Private option and SOC2 artifact location.
- Performance knobs: suggested batching settings, recommended model/quantization profile for cost/latency tradeoff.
- Runbook for debugging: log sample IDs to correlate requests, how to enable prefix/KV caching for repeated contexts.

Acme asked specifically for function calling JSON schema and a streaming example. I attached the integration diagram and a small code patch with sample SDK snippets. Please attach the patch back with any edits.

Thanks — Marissa
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alice Johnson <alice.johnson@acme.com>, Tom Wu <tom.wu@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Oct 2026 15:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ACME POC - Integration plan, success criteria, and next steps

Thanks — tagging an implementation plan and timeline below. I’ll be the engineering lead for the POC; Lauren will own QA and rollout support.

Quick plan (high level) + deliverables:
- Dev spike (1-2 days) - confirm test account, run sample prompts, validate token profiles.
- SDK examples (2 days) - add minimal snippets to repo and return patch: languages: Python and Node. Deliverable: redwood_sdk_sample_code.patch
  - Python example (requests):
    curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n      -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \n      -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n      -d '{"model":"redwood-1.0","input":"Summarize the following...","max_tokens":512}'

  - Streaming (SSE) example: connect to https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams with Authorization header. Server will send incremental chunks with event: token. Client should handle reconnect/backoff.

- Function calling: provide function schema template (JSON) and example payloads. Example contract:
  {"name":"create_ticket","arguments":{"title":"string","body":"string","priority":"string"}}
  Redwood will return a structured JSON payload when the model invokes the function. We will include a small Node sample demonstrating invocation and response parsing.

- API routes for the POC:
  - POST /v1/generate - synchronous text generation
  - POST /v1/streams - streaming responses (SSE)
  - POST /v1/embeddings - embedding vectors for re-ranking
  - POST /v1/functions/execute - optional function-call broker for secured outbound calls

- Auth/security: POC will use scoped API keys. For customers wanting Private deployment later, we support mTLS and customer-managed KMS (we will note this in the security doc). I will attach the SOC2 artifact link to the drive folder.

- Performance and cost guidance:
  - Recommended model: redwood-1.0-small quantized for low-latency; redwood-1.0-medium for higher quality.
  - Batching suggestions: continuous batching with 50ms collect window for request mix; enable prefix KV caching for repeated contexts.

Estimated timeline (calendar days from kickoff 2026-10-20):
- 2026-10-20 to 2026-10-21: Dev spike + SDK examples (2 days)
- 2026-10-22 to 2026-10-26: Integration and wiring (API + function-calling + streaming) (5 days)
- 2026-10-27 to 2026-10-29: Internal testing + fixups (3 days)

Owners:
- Dylan Brooks (dylan.brooks@redwood.ai) - implementation lead, SDK patch, endpoints
- Lauren Bishop (lauren.bishop@redwood.ai) - QA, test plan, evaluation scripts
- Marissa Cole - customer coordination and scheduling

Next steps:
- We will attach the SDK patch to this thread (redwood_sdk_sample_code.patch) and a short function-calling example JSON.
- Confirm kickoff 2026-10-20 at 10:00 PT (Marissa to send invite).

If that looks good I will push the patch and a short README to the Drive folder and we can kick off.

\u0014Dylan
Lead Engineer, Integrations | Redwood Inference
